summary.headline: Q1 FY27 revenue rose 37% YoY to INR4,490 million and EBITDA to INR1,233 million (+39% YoY); FY28 guidance of $400M revenue and 40% margin reiterated.
summary.overview: Revenue of INR4,490 million grew 37% YoY, driven by the semaglutide commercial launch, new MSA contracts and new customer wins. EBITDA of INR1,233 million rose 39% YoY and 34% QoQ, with management attributing the margin step-up mainly to a higher drug-device combination (DDC) contribution. Management said capacity is full, with the second cartridge line commissioning this quarter and a third line due within FY27. FY28 guidance of $400 million organic revenue and 40% EBITDA margin was reiterated.

financial_highlights.change: Each new line doubles sterile days

segments.name: Drug-device combination (DDC)
segments.commentary: Main driver of the margin improvement; second cartridge line commissioning this quarter, third line within FY27, and a fourth later in FY28. Management says existing cartridge capacity is fully utilised while pre-filled syringe capacity is largely available.

segments.name: Biologics
segments.commentary: Added Formycon (biosimilars) and an animal-health contract; RFP funnel is almost 4x what it was just over a year ago. Commercial revenue expected from FY29 onward, with mammalian and microbial capacity expansion under consideration.

segments.name: Soft gelatin
segments.commentary: Capacity expanded from 800 million to 2.4 billion units; the business is shifting from captive Strides IP to CDMO. Management expects the added capacity to be fully taken up over 12-15 months and has started a greenfield site process.

segments.name: Injectables (Steri-Science)
segments.commentary: Focused portfolio built around penicillin and FDA-shortage products. A sterile injectable site shutdown starts in Q2 and runs into Q3 to add pre-filled syringe and lyophilisation capacity.

guidance_outlook: FY28 guidance reiterated: US$400 million organic revenue and 40% EBITDA margin; Q&A cites US$160 million EBITDA.
EBITDA trajectory expected to keep rising beyond FY28, with Europe and US (FTF) volumes opening from FY29-30.
Revenue and EBITDA expected to grow sequentially QoQ through FY27, with H2 weighted by new-line ramp-up and soft gel seasonality.
Opex already upfronted, so the full contribution from new lines is expected once all lines are in place.
Capex beyond the US$100 million programme for biologics expected to be significantly lower than DDC spend.
capex_capacity: Second cartridge line to commission in Q1 FY27; batch sizes moving from ~200 L to ~500 L on lines to increase output per sterile day.
Third line to be ready within FY27; fourth line later in FY28. Management expects three lines fully available for FY28 (675 sterile days in total).
Soft gelatin is at its current site capacity limit; a greenfield site is being initiated, with an update expected in about one quarter.
Injectables shutdown in Q2-Q3 FY27 for pre-filled syringe and lyophilisation additions; benefit expected in FY28.
Around 80% of the US$100 million capex is committed; the remaining ~20% is the balance.
demand_pricing: Management says all current capacity is full, and demand is pulled forward to offset temporary supply disruption at Dr. Reddy's, with no supply impact expected.

Semaglutide generics: all three Canadian approvals held; two partners launched; over 40% of India's generic pen market is made at the site. Indian generic pen volumes rose from under 2,000 a month to 150,000-160,000.
Management says the mix will shift toward commercial supply (CSA) over MSAs as the new lines come online.
Six new logos and nine launches added in the quarter; a new GLP customer was onboarded last quarter.
First oncology soft gel NDA secured with a top-10 US generic; management described the market as small with no significant near-term revenue.

qa_highlights.question: Why has soft gel revenue not grown faster after capacity went from 800 million to 2.4 billion units?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the business was captive under Strides and is now shifting to CDMO, with tech transfers taking time. It expects the added capacity to be fully taken over 12-15 months and has started a greenfield site process.

qa_highlights.question: Did the injectable shutdown affect Q1, and what drove the sequential margin improvement?
qa_highlights.answer: The injectable shutdown starts this quarter and runs into Q2. The margin rise was attributed mainly to higher DDC contribution plus soft gel and injectable seasonality, which is H2-weighted.

qa_highlights.question: Is there order book visibility to achieve the $400 million FY28 target?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said yes, citing DDC order book, biologics new contracts and funnel, soft gel customer additions and new injectable capabilities.

qa_highlights.question: Can the new lines be used for any customer, and will batch-size changes need regulatory approval?
qa_highlights.answer: Capacity is fungible across lines and customers; customers will be served from both lines. Batch size increases from 200 L to 500 L should be possible in most geographies with a quick approval, depending on the market.

qa_highlights.question: Did Q1 capture the full EBITDA contribution from line one?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said revenue from line one reached full per-line contribution in Q1, but profitability will improve only once all lines are installed, because most opex has already been upfronted.

qa_highlights.question: What is the capex outlook beyond the US$100 million programme?
qa_highlights.answer: About 80% of the US$100 million is committed. Biologics capacity expansion will need additional capex, expected to be significantly lower than DDC spend.

risks_watch: Dr. Reddy's temporary supply disruption: whether its supplies resume on the publicly stated timeline, and how it affects the pulled-forward demand.
Soft gel ramp-up pace versus the 12-15 month takeover estimate, plus the greenfield site decision and cost (update due in about one quarter).
Execution of line 2 (Q1) and line 3 (within FY27) commissioning, batch-size approvals, and whether opex leverage follows.
Geopolitical freight disruption (Suez and Strait of Hormuz) and new US tariff announcements on generics; management says CDMO exposure is limited because contracts are ex-works.
Biologics commercial revenue is largely expected only from FY29 onward, so FY28 depends on DDC, soft gel and injectables.
summary.management_tone: Confident and assertive on demand, capacity and FY28 targets, with management repeatedly stressing that capacity is full. Less specific on soft gel timelines, the greenfield site, and the injectable shutdown impact. Several answers deflected on capacity utilisation and CSA counts.
key_quotes: With all this, we really remain confident and are happy to reiterate our FY28 outlook of $400 million organic revenue as well as, EBITDA margins of 40%.
The constraint in this market has been supply, not demand.

Third DDC cartridge line, ready within FY27
Fourth DDC cartridge line later in FY28
Soft gelatin capacity expansion from 800 million to 2.4 billion units (already added)
Greenfield soft gelatin site, update expected in about one quarter
Injectables sterile site shutdown to add pre-filled syringe and lyophilisation capacity, Q2-Q3 FY27

growth.why: FY28 guidance of US$400M organic revenue and 40% EBITDA margin was reiterated, backed by a second cartridge line commissioning this quarter, a third line within FY27, a fourth later in FY28 (675 sterile days by FY28), and a US$100M capex programme ~80% committed; capacity is fully utilised and Q1 revenue grew 37% YoY, though the brief gives no line-by-line revenue bridge to FY28.
